tasks.title: Compose the rendered bytes, expose them, and write spec.md with every save
steps: Add the composition, determinism, exposure, failed-save and load behaviours to afspec/render_test.go and afspec/afspec_test.go, and confirm they fail

In afspec/render.go add the exported constant RenderedFileName = "spec.md" and an exported constant holding the header line verbatim: `<!-- Generated by afspec from prd.md, requirements.json, test_spec.json, tasks.json and architecture.md. Do not edit: change those files, or run speca <package> --render. -->`

In afspec/render.go add `func (s *Spec) RenderedBytes() []byte`, returning the header line, a newline, a blank line and then s.RenderCombined() with no RenderOption, so the bytes from the third line on are the unscoped, unbudgeted combined render

In saveToDisk in afspec/afspec.go append {name: RenderedFileName, data: s.RenderedBytes()} to the artifacts slice after the architecture.md entry, so spec.md goes through the same phase 1 temp write with fsync and the same phase 2 rename as the other artifacts, and a phase 1 failure still leaves every file as it was

Confirm Save, Transition and Supersede all reach it, and that Transition writes the render of the package it is about to persist, so the Status, Updated and Intent hash lines of the render hold the new values

In buildPackage in specgen/pipeline.go append afspec.RenderedFileName to pkg.Artifacts inside the write branch, after written is set, so that spec is honest about the files it wrote (envelope/spec_result.go: "Artifacts are the files written") and a dry run, which wrote none, does not list it

Fix the existing tests that enumerate what a save or a run wrote: the names slice of TestSave_RoundTripIsByteIdentical around afspec/afspec_test.go:88, the exact file list asserted around specgen/pipeline_test.go:879, and the artifacts assertion around specgen/pipeline_test.go:380; then grep the other test files for directory listings of a package and add spec.md where a package's files are enumerated

Document the two exported identifiers in docs/api.md, spec.md in the write in docs/architecture.md, and spec.md among a run's artifacts in docs/cli.md where it describes package.artifacts; run make doc

tasks.title: Report a render that is missing, unreadable or stale in the verdict
steps: Add the rendered-rule behaviours to afspec/validate_test.go and the refused activation to cmd/speca/status_test.go, and confirm they fail

In afspec/afspec.go give Spec an unexported boolean field that LoadSpec sets and nothing else does, recording that the package was read from disk; it is copied by value with the struct, so Transition and Supersede keep it, and a package specgen builds in memory for a dry run (specgen/pipeline.go sets Dir on such a package) does not have it

In afspec/validate.go add the rendered rule: do nothing unless the package was read from disk; read <Dir>/spec.md; when it does not exist, report one warning with Check "rendered", Artifact "spec.md" and a message saying spec.md is missing and naming `speca <package> --render`

When the file exists and cannot be read, or exists and its bytes differ from RenderedBytes(), report one entry with Check "rendered" and Artifact "spec.md": an error when Status is draft or active, a warning for sealed, superseded and archived; the message names the 1-based number of the first line that differs, or the read error when the read failed, and `speca <package> --render`
When the bytes are equal, report nothing at all under the rule

Call the rule from Spec.Validate in both of its branches — the early return for a schema-invalid package and the cross-file path — so that a package whose schemas fail is still told its render is stale, and append its findings to the errors or the warnings as the case above says

Fix the existing tests that assert the exact set of warnings or the exact count of findings for a fixture package (afspec/validate_test.go, cmd/speca/verdict_test.go, cmd/specr tests, specgen tests): a package on disk without a spec.md now carries one rendered warning

Confirm checkActivation in cmd/speca/status_checks.go refuses a draft package whose spec.md differs, because it asks the package's own validation, and that --force still activates it with the high spec_invalid warning naming the rendered rule

Document the rule in docs/speca.md, and in specification/spec-format-v2.md add spec.md to §3 as a generated file of the package that is not canonical and is never read as data, and the rule rendered to the §10.2 table with its draft-or-active error and its sealed warning
